title: Customer-Facing Throughput Commitment Matrix and Remediation Script
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a single customer-facing artifact (matrix + remediation script + sample clause language) that binds the Dedicated product's throughput commitments to measurable SLOs, a deterministic error-budget accounting method, and a playbook customers and CSMs can use when credits/notifications are triggered.

Scope: define latency envelopes (quantile and per-token), throughput windows (tokens/minute and sustained tokens/hour), crediting formulas, notification windows, remediation steps, and canned customer communications. Include an appendix with autoscaling interlock and fleet control constraints that affect crediting (AZ failovers, node rebalancing, kernel upgrades).

Decisions made so far:
- Offer two commitment tiers: Standard (best-effort with 95/50ms latency envelope for small sequences at provisioned RPS) and Enterprise (contracted tokens/minute with 99/100ms envelope and priority autoscale).
- Error budget defined as percentage of served tokens outside the latency envelope over a rolling 30-day window; credits computed proportional to the shortfall relative to committed throughput.
- Crediting formula chosen: proportional token-weighted credit with floor and cap (floor = 5% monthly credit, cap = 100% of one month of committed fee), math spelled out in appendix.
- Autoscaling interlock: automatic burst autoscale is deferred to Dedicated controller; credits do not apply when degradation is caused by customer misconfiguration or scheduled maintenance announced >72 hours.
- Fleet controls: AZ failover and planned kernel upgrades are excluded from crediting if documented in maintenance window; unplanned AZ outage is creditable.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Tighter latency envelopes reduce risk for customers but raise capacity cost to Redwood; decided to keep Standard tier conservative to avoid reserve costs for small accounts.
- Real-time per-tenant autoscale exposes operational and security complexity; chosen path: operator-only increasing of reserved pools with transparent visibility in Console.

Open questions / blockers:
- Legal review of sample contract language for notice windows and arbitration clauses (legal assigned but pending).
- Exact telemetry thresholds for determining "customer misconfiguration" will need ENG instrumentation changes (see dependencies).

Acceptance criteria (must be met before release):
- Final matrix published to Confluence and attached to billing/contract templates.
- Two example customer letters (notice + remediation) created and approved by Legal.
- Implementation notes for ENG containing metric names, alert thresholds, and crediting computation pseudocode.
- UX copy for Console's SLA dashboard wireframes reviewed by Design and included in rollout plan.

Links and artifacts:
- Draft matrix and playbook (Confluence): https://redwood.atl.confluence/dedicated/throughput-commitment-matrix-draft
- Design wireframes (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-wireframes
- Implementation PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345
- Billing credit formula spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-credit-formula
- Incident reference for previous degradation (INC-2026-0112) - postmortem: https://redwood.atl.confluence/incidents/INC-2026-0112-postmortem

Notes for ENG/OPS handoff:
- Metric names required: dedicated.serve.latency.p50_tokens, dedicated.serve.latency.p95_tokens, dedicated.serve.tokens_served_per_minute, dedicated.serve.error_budget_breach_count.
- Time windows: rolling 30d for error budget, 7d lookback for immediate notification thresholds.
- Crediting service will be a new microservice owned by Billing; pseudocode attached in PR.

Why this differs from previous artifacts: this ticket is customer-facing and prescriptive — it combines legal-friendly clause language, operations remediation script, and the exact telemetry-to-credit mapping so Sales/CSMs and customers have a single source of truth (instead of separate contract annexes and internal playbooks).
